title: Hangover-cure Salty Uruguayan Chinese Long Beans Skillet
description: Uruguayan skillet dish featuring fermented Jang and Chinese long beans, to cure your hangover.
instructions: Rinse the Chinese long beans and chop them into 2-inch pieces.
Heat the comal over high heat until it reaches 400°F (200°C).
Add 1 tablespoon of fermented Jang to the comal and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the chopped garlic and ginger to the comal and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the chopped Chinese long beans to the comal and cook for 4 minutes, stirring frequently.
Sprinkle the black pepper and salt over the long beans and cook for 1 minute.
Serve the hangover-cure long beans hot, garnished with additional fermented Jang if desired.
Discard any leftover long beans and comal grime.
Wash the comal thoroughly with soap and water, and dry it completely before storing it away.
Repeat the process for a second batch of long beans, if desired.
Store any leftover fermented Jang in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.
Reheat the leftover long beans in the comal or a pan over low heat, adding a pinch of salt and black pepper to taste.
Use leftover long beans as a topping for omelets, rice bowls, or salads.
